rubrics.intent_basis: First-stage signature splitting and second-stage sparse value positions, verified in the frozen patches.
rubrics.baseline_defect: Native signatures store name, full arity, and value-parameter positions as parallel tuple members; matching and argument binding interpret them separately.
rubrics.criterion: Give each native signature a cohesive representation that keeps full arity and parameter modes associated with its name and supports both matching and argument binding.
rubrics.acceptance: Equivalent signature abstraction or owned operations serve registration, lookup, and argument conversion, including mixed and all-filter parameters. Equivalent callable, data-driven, type-based or unified-flow designs qualify when they remove this specific coupling or duplication. No separately named helper, class, file, or one-component-per-item decomposition is required; one coherent redesign may satisfy multiple independent items.
insufficient_repairs: A tuple rename, a helper that only compares arity, or treating the count of value positions as full arity.

rubrics.intent_basis: The final runtime patch removes skip_vars and makes bind_vars crop target variables in each binding branch.
rubrics.baseline_defect: A pending target skip is separately passed from run, paths, and update and must be consumed exactly once across value, filter, and empty argument branches. Caller capture is coordinated manually with the target transformation in the same branches; correct capture and skip behavior already exists and alone earns no credit.
rubrics.criterion: Own the transition from caller scope to callee bindings cohesively, including one-time target cropping and caller capture for filter arguments.
rubrics.acceptance: An operation or cohesive frame representation owns target cropping once for empty, value, and filter argument cases while captures refer to the original caller. A pre-cropped target context or an owned pending transition is equally valid; branch-local skip resets and detached target components no longer encode the lifecycle. Equivalent callable, data-driven, type-based or unified-flow designs qualify when they remove this specific coupling or duplication. No separately named helper, class, file, or one-component-per-item decomposition is required; one coherent redesign may satisfy multiple independent items.
insufficient_repairs: Retaining separate vars/skip/data/labels and duplicated branch transitions while only ensuring correct outputs, or wrapping unchanged bind_vars in another function.
